region.sunny-meadow.name: Sunny Meadow
quest.snack-5: Give 5 right answers at snack time
word.equal-groups.nests: {name} finds {nests} nests. Each nest has {eggs} eggs. How many eggs are there?
word.equal-groups.bikes: There are {bikes} bikes at school. Each bike has {wheels} wheels. How many wheels are there?
word.equal-groups.stars: {name} draws {stars} stars. Each star has {points} points. How many points are there?
word.equal-groups.crayons: {name} has {packs} packs of crayons. Each pack has {each} crayons. How many crayons are there?
word.equal-groups.baskets: {name} fills {baskets} baskets. Each basket has {each} {things}. How many {things} are there?
word.equal-groups.clovers: {name} finds {clovers} clovers. Each clover has {leaves} leaves. How many leaves are there?
word.equal-groups.dragons: {count} baby dragons sleep in a cave. Each dragon has {legs} legs. How many legs are there?
word.equal-groups.eggs: Grandma buys {boxes} boxes of eggs. Each box has {each} eggs. How many eggs does she buy?
word.equal-groups.weeks: A week has {days} days. How many days are in {weeks} weeks?
word.equal-groups.beetles: {name} sees {beetles} beetles. Each beetle has {legs} legs. How many legs are there?
word.equal-groups.rainbows: {name} paints {count} rainbows. Each rainbow has {colours} colours. How many colours are there?
word.equal-groups.spiders: {count} spiders live in the cave. Each spider has {legs} legs. How many legs are there?
word.equal-groups.gems: The Gnome King has {rows} rows of gems. Each row has {each} gems. How many gems are there?
word.equal-groups.market: At the market, {name} buys {bags} bags. Each bag has {each} {things}. How many {things} does {name} buy?
word.equal-groups.tickets: A ticket to the castle costs {price} Kč. How much do {count} tickets cost?
word.equal-groups.pencils: Each pack has {each} pencils. The school buys {packs} packs. How many pencils is that?
word.equal-groups.books: A big book has {pages} pages. How many pages do {count} books have?
word.equal-groups.trucks: A truck carries {each} sacks of potatoes. How many sacks do {trucks} trucks carry?
word.sharing.berries: {name} has {total} berries and {baskets} baskets. Each basket gets the same number. How many berries go in each basket?
word.sharing.friends: {name} and {friend} share {total} {things} fairly. How many {things} does each child get?
word.sharing.pancakes: Dad makes {total} pancakes for {plates} plates. Each plate gets the same number. How many pancakes go on each plate?
word.sharing.plums: {dragons} dragons share {total} plums fairly. How many plums does each dragon get?
word.sharing.gnomes: The Gnome King shares {total} gems among {gnomes} gnomes. Each gnome gets the same number. How many gems does each gnome get?
word.sharing.class: The teacher shares {total} {things} fairly among {children} children. How many {things} does each child get?
word.sharing.books: The school has {total} new books for {classes} classes. Each class gets the same number. How many books does each class get?
word.sharing.giant: The giant shares {total} apples among {friends} friends. Each friend gets the same number. How many apples does each friend get?
word.grouping.bags: {name} has {total} {things}. She puts {each} in each bag. How many bags does she fill?
word.grouping.teams: {total} children play a game. They make teams of {size}. How many teams are there?
word.grouping.eggs: Grandpa has {total} eggs. He puts {each} eggs in each box. How many boxes does he fill?
word.grouping.holiday: {name}'s holiday is {days} days long. A week has {week} days. How many weeks is the holiday?
word.grouping.spiders: {name} counts {legs} spider legs. Each spider has {each} legs. How many spiders are there?
word.grouping.chests: The gnomes have {total} gems. They put {each} gems in each chest. How many chests do they fill?
word.grouping.market: {name} has {total} {things}. He sells them in bags of {each}. How many bags can he fill?
word.grouping.giant: {total} children visit the giant. They walk in groups of {size}. How many groups are there?
word.times-as-many.fruit: {name} has {small} {thing}. {friend} has {times} times as many. How many does {friend} have?
word.times-as-many.sparks: Ember breathes {small} sparks. Rainbow breathes {times} times as many. How many sparks does Rainbow breathe?
word.times-as-many.treasure: {name} finds {small} {thing}. The Gnome King finds {times} times as many. How many does the Gnome King find?
word.times-as-many.pond: {name} sees {small} {thing} in the pond. Grandpa sees {times} times as many. How many does Grandpa see?
word.times-as-many.savings: {name} saves {small} Kč. {friend} saves {times} times as many. How many crowns does {friend} save?
word.times-fewer.fruit: {name} has {total} {things}. {name} has {times} times as many as {friend}. How many {things} does {friend} have?
word.times-fewer.scales: Rainbow has {total} shiny scales. Rainbow has {times} times as many as Ember. How many scales does Ember have?
word.times-fewer.treasure: The Gnome King has {total} {things}. The king has {times} times as many as {name}. How many {things} does {name} have?
word.times-fewer.pond: Grandpa catches {total} fish. Grandpa catches {times} times as many as {name}. How many fish does {name} catch?
word.more-than.flowers: {name} picks {picked} flowers. {friend} picks {more} more. How many flowers does {friend} pick?
word.more-than.fruit: {name} has {small} {thing}. {friend} has {more} more. How many does {friend} have?
word.more-than.inverse: {name} has {total} {things}. {name} has {more} more than {friend}. How many {things} does {friend} have?
word.more-than.plums: Ember eats {eaten} plums. Rainbow eats {more} more. How many plums does Rainbow eat?
word.fewer-than.fruit: {name} has {total} {things}. {friend} has {fewer} fewer. How many does {friend} have?
word.fewer-than.inverse: {name} has {small} {thing}. {name} has {fewer} fewer than {friend}. How many {things} does {friend} have?
word.fewer-than.class: There are {count} girls in the class. There are {fewer} fewer boys. How many boys are there?
word.leftover.bags: {name} has {total} {things}. She puts {size} in each bag. How many bags can she fill? How many are left over?
word.leftover.boats: {total} children want a boat ride. Each boat takes {size} children. How many boats are full? How many children are left over?
word.leftover.necklaces: The Lake Nymphs have {total} pearls. They make necklaces of {size} pearls. How many necklaces can they make? How many pearls are left?
word.leftover.plates: {name} bakes {total} {things}. He puts {size} on each plate. How many plates are full? How many are left?
word.leftover.album: {name} has {total} stickers. Each album page holds {size} stickers. How many pages can {name} fill? How many stickers are left?
word.two-step.bags: {name} buys {bags} bags of {things}. Each bag has {each} {things}. {name} eats {eaten} {thing}. How many {things} are left?
word.two-step.tickets: A ticket costs {price} Kč. {name} buys {count} tickets. {name} pays {paid} Kč. How many crowns does {name} get back?
word.two-step.chairs: There are {rows} rows of chairs. Each row has {each} chairs. {kids} children sit down. How many chairs are empty?
word.two-step.bowls: {name} picks {plums} plums and {pears} pears. She shares them fairly between {bowls} bowls. How many are in each bowl?
word.two-step.pocket: {name} has {start} Kč. {name} buys {count} {things} for {price} Kč each. How many crowns are left?
word.two-step.stickers: {name} has {packs} packs of {each} stickers. {name} gives {given} stickers to {friend}. How many stickers does {name} have now?
word.two-step.garden: {name} plants {rows} rows of carrots. Each row has {each} carrots. Then {name} plants {more} more carrots. How many carrots are there?
story.prologue.1: Long ago, a dragon with seven heads caught a cold.
story.prologue.2: A-choo! The Magic Window broke into shiny pieces.
story.prologue.3: All the dragon eggs in the valley went cold.
story.prologue.4: Old Glimmer needs a new Dragon Keeper. You are the one!
story.first-egg.choose: Choose your first egg. Which one feels warm?
story.first-egg.chosen: Great choice! Let's warm it up with some practice.
story.meadow-welcome.1: Welcome to Sunny Meadow! The flowers love counting.
story.meadow-welcome.2: Dragons hatch when you practise. Let's begin!
story.meadow-new-eggs.1: Look! Two new eggs: a silver one and a cloudy one.
story.meadow-new-eggs.2: Ones and zeros will warm them up.
story.bridge-troll.1: A big troll sits on the old bridge.
story.bridge-troll.2: He grumbles and will not let anyone cross.
story.bridge-troll.3: Glimmer whispers: make him laugh with your answers!
story.troll-laughs.1: The troll laughs so hard that he rolls over!
story.troll-laughs.2: The bridge is open. New adventures are waiting!

quest.snack-10: Give 10 right answers at snack time
story.whispering-woods-welcome.1: Welcome to Whispering Woods! The trees count in threes.
story.whispering-woods-welcome.2: Look, a green egg with three spots. It is Clover's!
story.whispering-woods-welcome.3: Practise threes and fours to warm it up.
story.forest-witch.1: The Forest Witch blocks the path with her broom.
story.forest-witch.2: She loves puzzles more than anything.
story.forest-witch.3: Solve her puzzles, and she will agree!
story.witch-agrees.1: The witch claps her hands. You solved them all!
story.witch-agrees.2: She shares her gingerbread heart. The path is open!
story.fire-mountain-welcome.1: Welcome to Fire Mountain! The rocks are warm here.
story.fire-mountain-welcome.2: This egg has six little spikes. It is Ember's!
story.fire-mountain-welcome.3: Sixes and sevens will make it hatch.
story.krakonos.1: Krakonoš, the Mountain Spirit, sends grey clouds.
story.krakonos.2: He has not laughed for a hundred years.
story.krakonos.3: Warm his heart with sixes and sevens!
story.krakonos-laughs.1: Krakonoš laughs! The clouds roll away.
story.krakonos-laughs.2: The sun shines on the mountain path again.
story.crystal-caves-welcome.1: Welcome to Crystal Caves! Everything sparkles in the dark.
story.crystal-caves-welcome.2: Here is an icy egg. It belongs to Crystal!
story.crystal-caves-welcome.3: Eights and nines will warm it up.
story.gnome-king.1: The Gnome King guards his shiny gems.
story.gnome-king.2: He wants them sorted in eights and nines.
story.gnome-king.3: Help him sort, and he will agree to help you!
story.gnome-king-dances.1: The Gnome King shows you his biggest crystal.
story.gnome-king-dances.2: Then he dances a happy gnome dance!
story.sharing-lake-welcome.1: Welcome to Sharing Lake! Here everyone shares fairly.
story.sharing-lake-welcome.2: Your dragons grow bigger when you divide.
story.water-goblin.1: The Water Goblin keeps fruit in his teacups.
story.water-goblin.2: He gives it back only when it is shared fairly.
story.goblin-agrees.1: The Water Goblin smiles and lifts his teacups.
story.goblin-agrees.2: Fruit for everyone! The lake path is open.
story.leftover-lagoon-welcome.1: Welcome to Leftover Lagoon! Some things do not share evenly.
story.leftover-lagoon-welcome.2: Leftovers stay in the bowl. Pearl loves leftovers.
story.leftover-lagoon-welcome.3: Look, here is Pearl's shiny egg!
story.lake-nymphs.1: Three Lake Nymphs dance on the water.
story.lake-nymphs.2: They want to count their leftover pearls.
story.lake-nymphs.3: Help them, and they will laugh and dance!
story.nymphs-laugh.1: The nymphs laugh and spin around you.
story.nymphs-laugh.2: Their pearls sparkle. The way to the peaks is open!
story.giants-peaks-welcome.1: Welcome to Giant's Peaks! Everything here is big.
story.giants-peaks-welcome.2: This heavy egg is Boulder's. Boulder carries big numbers.
story.giants-peaks-welcome.3: Let us try numbers bigger than the tables!
story.friendly-giant.1: A giant sits on the mountain top.
story.friendly-giant.2: He is friendly, but very, very busy.
story.friendly-giant.3: Calm him with big answers, and he will rest.
story.giant-sleeps.1: The giant yawns a giant yawn.
story.giant-sleeps.2: He falls asleep, smiling. Let him sleep and walk on quietly!
story.riddle-ruins-welcome.1: Welcome to Riddle Ruins! Old gears turn in order.
story.riddle-ruins-welcome.2: Here is Clockwork's brass egg. Tick, tock!
story.riddle-ruins-welcome.3: Here, the order of the steps matters.
story.golem.1: The Golem is a big helper made of clay.
story.golem.2: He only moves when the steps come in order.
story.golem.3: Tell him what to do first!
story.golem-agrees.1: The Golem nods. One step at a time, in the right order!
story.golem-agrees.2: He opens the gate to Dragon Castle.
story.dragon-castle-welcome.1: Welcome to Dragon Castle! The Magic Window is here.
story.dragon-castle-welcome.2: The Seven-Headed Dragon is still sneezing.
story.dragon-castle-welcome.3: Let us practise everything you know!
story.seven-headed.1: Seven heads, seven sneezes! Achoo, achoo, achoo!
story.seven-headed.2: Each head needs a different kind of problem.
story.seven-headed.3: Three right answers cure one head.
story.finale.1: All seven heads smile at once. No more sneezes!
story.finale.2: The Magic Window shines, whole again.
story.finale.3: Look! The Seven-Headed Dragon is your friend now.
story.finale.4: Thank you, Dragon Keeper. The valley is warm again.

word.add-to.pebbles: {name} has {have} pebbles. {name} finds {more} more. How many pebbles now?
word.add-to.ducks: {swim} ducks swim. {more} more ducks come. How many ducks now?
word.take-from.frogs: {frogs} frogs sit on a stone. {jump} frogs jump away. How many frogs stay?
word.take-from.cherries: {name} has {total} cherries. {name} eats {eaten}. How many are left?
story.pebble-brook-welcome.2: Three eggs sleep by the water.
story.pebble-brook-welcome.choose: Choose your first egg. Which one is warm?
story.pebble-brook-welcome.chosen: Great choice! Let's warm it up.
story.will-o-wisps.1: Tiny lights float over the brook.
story.will-o-wisps.3: Count with them. Then they dance!
